**Subjective**
Anthony Dimarcello is a 40 year old male who presents for an annual preventive exam.
1. Housing: HB shelter since 9/2022
2. Medical history: denies chronic conditions
3. Surgical history: denies
4. Medications: denies
5. Social history: reports unemployed d/t injury
1. Reports h/o fractured ribs (per records ribs 3-6)
2. Reports used to work as a broker for federal govt and notes falsely arrested for identity theft
1. Reports incarcerated twice
6. Illicit drug use: denies
7. Alcohol: denies
8. tobacco use: social
Anthony also presents with the following additional problems:
Pt reports around last Spring/Summer he almost got hit by a car while riding his E-bike. Pt reports he has been seen multiple times at the hospital and has had Xrays. Pt notes his social worker put him on medical general relief. Pt reports he is now trying to get general relief form filled again. Pt reports he is not seeing a specialist but has done 1 session of PT which he states is paying out of pocket. Pt notes he plans to return to PT again and declines using insurance for PT referral. Overall pt notes intermittent sensation of "tightness" in left ribs. Denies fevers, chills, CP, SOB, nausea, vomit, diarrhea
- Hoag 3/24/23: dx-Multiple fractures of ribs, left side/ Contusion of right lower leg
- "Patient presents with left chest wall pain, left shoulder pain, and right lower extremity pain s/p fall off of an E bike 24 hours ago. No head injury or loss of consciousness. Patient attempted self-medication with marijuana with minimal relief. Chest wall pain exacerbated by inspiration and movement. Patient is hemodynamically stable with an SPO2 of 98% on room air. No significant overlying abrasions or ecchymosis but definite pain on palpation of ribs. No palpable crepitus. Patient has left shoulder pain without obvious deformity or edema. X-ray unremarkable for fracture or dislocation. Right lower extremity has a hematoma and abrasion. No evidence of foreign body, fracture, or dislocation per x-ray. Chest CT shows 4 rib fractures which 2 were mildly displaced.
0319 Cardiothoracic's consulted and case reviewed. Recommends outpatient follow-up and pain medication. Attempted to reevaluate patient and discussed disposition but patient eloped from ED. "
- Hoag 3/28/23
- "Patient returns the emergency department with reported difficulty breathing and sensation of fluid in lungs. I saw this patient during his last visit s/p E bike injury with subsequent rib fractures. At that time there was no evidence of pulmonary contusion, pneumothorax, hemothorax, or pleural effusion. Cardiothoracic was consulted during that visit who recommended outpatient follow-up but patient had eloped prior to formal discharge discussion. Today he is afebrile with mild tachycardia and moderate pain. Lungs are still clear on exam. Chest x-ray shows trace pleural effusion. Cardiothoracic's reconsulted who still recommends outpatient follow-up. Patient given an incentive spirometer with education as well as appropriate pain medication. Discussed suggested outpatient follow-up as well as precautions. "
- Hoag 6/9/23
- "He states he rested for 3 weeks and felt ok on motrin. Over the past 2 weeks has been doing more lifting of boxes and feels his left rib pain is aggravated, no repeat trauma. Also complains of left dental pain that he thinks was from initial e-bike fall
1936 CXR NAD
2004 Patient initially stating he never filled Rx from last visit however CURES states it was filled, patient then states he actually took the drug back to the pharmacy because it wasn't norco and concerned it
wasn't the same medication he got in the ED. Concern for pain seeking behavior. He can f/u with SOS clinic to establish primary care for referral to thoracic surgery and needs follow up with a dentist "
